newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian unions boycott Cairo's economic meet.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian unions boycott Cairo's economic meet.

text.p: Palestinian trade unions will boycott this month's Middle East economic conference in Cairo to protest at Israeli measures that are strangling their economy, union members said on Monday.
Representatives of the unions met last Wednesday and decided they would not send official delegations to the economic conference scheduled for November 12-14, the members said.
The Palestinian Authority is expected to send representatives to the conference. Some Palestinian businessmen said they would participate as private individuals.

"All the unions have decided to boycott the Middle East economic conference in Cairo as an expression of protest against Israeli measures which continue to suffocate our economy and have harmed our businesses," Adnan Faramant, owner of the Arab Food Company and a leading member of the food industrialists union, told Reuters.
"We see no reason for our participation as long as these measures are imposed and we continue to suffer from them."

Palestinian businessmen say that national industries and businesses have deteriorated as a result of closures on the West Bank and Gaza Strip beginning in 1994 which have only been eased intermittently.
They said the closures have increased unemployment in Gaza and the West Bank to over 50 percent and reduced per capita income by 35 percent. Many industries have had to lower production or shut down.
"As a result of the closures, Palestinian goods and people don't have freedom of movement to Israel, but Israel drowns our market with its goods," Faramant said.
